title: Shopping-relevant review synthesis — prompt v1.7.0; unchanged field contract
description: A shopping profile describing the user's circumstances, product use and selection criteria, grounded in the supplied reviews with concrete content.

main_category.description: The main category used to select the history. It does not guarantee that every review body discusses the same product format.

equipment.description: Reported tools/devices used with products and their limitations.

environment.description: Reported facilities, space, surroundings or local services relevant to using or choosing products.

people.description: Stated relationships and relevant information about other people involved in shopping or use.

personal_conditions.description: Directly reported personal needs, capabilities, sensitivities or constraints relevant to choosing or using products; preserve attribution and historical uncertainty.

history_statistics.description: Program-computed listed-price statistics for the history. These are not payment amounts, budgets, or unit prices.

usage_patterns.description: How the person buys, prepares, uses, stores and repurchases these products, at the level the evidence supports: a stated routine or repeated accounts support a pattern; one episode stays one episode; a plan stays a plan. General use suggestions are not usage records.

brand.description: Attitudes toward named brands, product lines or products: favorites and avoidances. A favorite or avoided product is named as that product, not its whole brand.

price.description: Price sensitivity, value judgments, willingness to pay and trade-offs against other aspects, from the person's words. Not inference from listed-price statistics.

review.description: Attitudes toward and use of other people's product reviews as information, including limited trust or criticism. Do not infer rating-caused purchases.

functional.description: Criteria about contents, ingredients, materials, specifications, compatibility, size, packaging, preparation effort and performance.

subjective.description: Criteria about experienced qualities: taste, aroma, texture, sound, comfort, appearance and style. Noticing a quality is not wanting it.

for_whom.description: The intended product user/beneficiary, not the attitude-holder. State the actor or attitude-holder in behavior/preference. A buyer's preference for a gift recipient is not automatically the recipient's own preference. The user by default for the writer's own use; null only when the passage concerns no particular person.

when.description: Relevant time, season or occasion. For usage: from a reported activity or explicitly stated plan. For preferences: a condition the person states for their own attitude, not necessarily an experienced event; a suggested use is not such a condition. null if unstated.

where.description: The explicitly stated location where the product is used or selected. null if unstated.

purpose.description: Stated aim/intended use of the activity or criterion; a suggested use of the product is not the person's aim. Do not restate the behavior or invent a motive. null if unstated.

reviews.description: Verbatim review_title/review_text spans supporting retained claims, linked to actual assigned record IDs. Code-generated price statistics instead cite source_header.

quote.description: A passage excerpted verbatim from the input history. Do not write an interpreted sentence or insert ellipses as if it were original text.

evidence_type.description: Classify the actual quoted span consistently, regardless of the section citing it: explicit_preference = stated taste/choice criterion; aspect_evaluation = evaluation of aspect(s), performance or scoped use outcome; product_description = observation without an evaluative stance; overall_evaluation = attitude to a whole product, including textual overall rating, never all its attributes; fact_or_usage = reported personal circumstance/activity/experience/concrete intention; metadata = program-only statistics. Focus spans where possible. For indivisible mixed spans use priority explicit_preference > aspect_evaluation > overall_evaluation > fact_or_usage > product_description. Label alone does not determine section placement or guarantee support.

review_count.description: Program-computed number of distinct supporting review IDs.

scope.description: The product or product/use range the activity covers, as far as its evidence reaches. Do not repeat the full main category; null if unsupported.

behavior.description: State the actor and the reported act, experience or concrete intention, with supported method/frequency. Distinguish a habit, occasional action, one episode and a plan. No habit inference from present tense alone.

scope.description: The products the attitude ranges over: for a criterion, what the person is choosing among (the product type unless they narrow it in their own words); for a single evaluation of one product, that product. Whatever makes the person prefer one product over another is the preference, never the scope; occasions, purposes and recipients go in context; reviewed products are evidence. Name the product type briefly rather than the full category path.

preference.description: State the attitude-holder, the concrete aspect they judged, the result they want, and any exception, accepted compromise, condition or change. It must hold for all cited evidence. Not a value word such as quality or reliability.

strength.description: required: an explicit necessity/exclusion in this scope and situation; preferred: a like/dislike, relative choice, named favorite or aspect satisfaction/dissatisfaction; unspecified: attitude is supported but its requirement level is unclear. Counts, routine and enthusiasm do not make it required; not a task scoring rule.
